{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises
premise_1 = (df['customer_segment'] == 'new').any() and (df['channel'] == 'paid_search').any()
premise_2 = df['channel'].isin(['email', 'paid_search']).all()
premise_3 = df['converted'].isin([0, 1]).all()

print(f"Premise 1 (new customers and paid_search exist): {premise_1}")
print(f"Premise 2 (channel only has email/paid_search): {premise_2}")
print(f"Premise 3 (converted is 0 or 1): {premise_3}")

# Filter for new customers reached by paid search
total_new_paid_search = len(df[(df['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (df['customer_segment'] == 'new')])
print(f"Total number of new customers reached by paid search: {total_new_paid_search}")

# Now, compute conversion rate over the full population: all new customers reached by paid search
# Conversion is defined as 'converted' == 1, regardless of status
# But note: if an order was refunded, it may still have been converted (i.e., completed checkout)
# The 'converted' column is 1 if checkout was completed, even if later refunded
# So we do NOT exclude refunded orders for conversion calculation

# Count total converted among all new customers reached by paid search
converted_count = df[(df['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (df['customer_segment'] == 'new') & (df['converted'] == 1)].shape[0]

# Compute fraction
fraction_converted = converted_count / total_new_paid_search

print(f"Number of converted orders among new customers reached by paid search: {converted_count}")
print(f"Fraction converted: {fraction_converted:.4f}")"}
